The device should now reboot itself and connect to the specific Wi-Fi/MQTT broker. \n\nWhen the connection succeeds, the device LED will turn solid green. That means the device has paired successfully. If that does not happen, then you need to start over again and double-check the Wi-Fi, MQTT and credential configuration.
Congratulations! The pairing process completed successfully and the HTTP API reported the device online. You should be ready to go.

Put your Meross device in Pairing mode and then tap on the update button.\n\nBe sure to enable both Wi-Fi and Location (GPS) access on your device. Some devices also require turning off the hotspot if it is enabled.
Please select the Wi-Fi AP where the Meross device should connect to.
Log-in to the HTTP API broker.
Make sure the Meross Local Broker add-on in Home Assistant is started, then log in with the credentials configured in that add-on.

Use this option to set the User ID and Key manually. These values are normally provided by the Meross Local Broker add-on. Only set them manually when pairing with a third-party broker and when you know what you are doing.
Pairs Meross devices with a local MQTT broker instead of the Meross cloud. Use it once per device; Home Assistant then controls the device on your local network.
Version %1$s is available on GitHub. You are running %2$s.

Meross Local Pairer is an independent fork of Custom Pairer for Meross Devices, originally created by Alberto Geniola. This fork is maintained by mazkagaz and has substantial changes: Bluetooth LE provisioning for devices that expose it, TLS, local-only login, trusted Wi-Fi handling, device revocation and re-claiming, a simplified setup and a redesigned interface. The MRS100 is the primary test target; other Meross models are welcome, and reports are useful.\n\nAlberto Geniola also wrote the original Meross low-level library and documentation. Icons: Freepik (flaticon.com).

• Not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Meross or the original author. Meross is a trademark of its owner.
• Local only: no Meross cloud account, no ads, no tracking, no telemetry.
• Credentials are stored encrypted on the phone. Device names and identifiers stay in your local broker.
• Open source under GPL-2.0. Provided as is, without warranty. Pairing changes the device configuration; use at your own risk.
This app is free and open source. If it helps you, you can report issues, suggest improvements or contribute code on GitHub.
